pr.title: Leave a cancelled run's checks out of CHECKS and the panel's checks, and note a draft a hold shadows
pr.head: 829877fdf2c5bc694163c1bbd974ae499a9817ad

summary: Projector reads a pull request's CI results in two places. The watch daemon, a background process that polls each pull request a session subscribes to, sends a CHECKS event to the session that fixes the pull request when a check fails. The panel, the list of pull requests Projector draws in Claude Code, colors a row failing and its drawer reads checks failing. Both read GitHub's check rollup: every check run and commit status on the head commit, with counts by state.

Some repositories start CI on GitHub's labeled event and cancel a pull request's earlier run when a new one starts (concurrency: cancel-in-progress). A review adds the reviewing label when it starts, so each review cancels the run in progress. GitHub keeps the cancelled run's checks on the head beside the newer run's, and a job that runs if: always() to gather the others fails in the cancelled run. So the daemon and the panel reported a failure that no code caused.

This change leaves a failed check run out when its check suite, the record GitHub keeps for one workflow run, concluded CANCELLED. The daemon drops it from CHECKS, and the panel moves it from failing into a new cancelled bucket, so a head with only a cancelled run's checks reads checks cancelled. The panel also notes cancelled on a row while a workflow's newest run on the head was cancelled, and notes draft when another status takes a draft's word. docs/cli.md gains a section on keeping review labels from cancelling CI runs.

cards.title: What the review found
cards.html:
The Projector review of 829877f opened two threads. Both come from one choice: the rule reads the workflow run's conclusion and not what each job did.

  • A real failure is hidden. A job that failed on its own before a newer run cancelled its run is dropped too, so when the newer run skips that job, neither CHECKS nor the panel reports the failure.
  • A cancelled-only head can read passing. A job that passed before the cancel still counts as passing, so the drawer reads checks passing where docs/plugins.md says checks cancelled.

groups.title: The daemon leaves a cancelled run's failures out of CHECKS
groups.kicker: How the watch daemon decides which failed checks to report
intro: The daemon's query now asks for each check run's suite conclusion and, for the panel, the workflow run's workflow and start time. failures keeps the old rule for what counts as a failure. failed_contexts, which names the checks in a CHECKS event, then drops each failure whose suite concluded CANCELLED.

The daemon reads the first 20 rollup contexts and pages further only while the rollup's counts hold a failure it has not read. It still pages by the raw count from failures, so a cancelled run's failure on the first page stops the paging rather than sending it through every page looking for a failure it will drop.

files.note: Splits the old failure filter into failures and failed_contexts, and adds in_cancelled_run.

checks.text: Open review finding: in_cancelled_run reads only the workflow run's conclusion, so a job that failed on its own before a newer run cancelled its run is dropped too. Where the newer run skips that job, as a label run whose jobs skip for other labels does, CHECKS reports nothing where the base reported the failure.

The paging loop counts every failure, cancelled-run ones included, so the nodes the daemon writes to its cache hold every failure the counts hold. The panel's subtraction reads those nodes, so it finds each cancelled-run failure the daemon found. Checked by reading read_contexts and the new paging test.

files.note: Two tests: a cancelled run's failure next to a passing newer run sends no event while a real failure beside it still does, and a cancelled run's failure on the first page reads no later page.

groups.title: The panel computes checks from the counts, less a cancelled run's failures
groups.kicker: How the panel turns the rollup into one checks state
intro: checksOf used to fall back to the rollup's own state unless the projector/review status was present. It now always counts by state, takes out the review status, and moves each failed check run of a cancelled suite from failing to cancelled. The state is the first of failing, pending, passing, and cancelled that has a count, so cancelled shows only when nothing else ran.

cancelledOf finds each workflow's newest run on the head by its start time and sets isCancelled when any of those was cancelled. The panel's own query, used for pull requests the daemon has no result for, now reads the first 20 contexts with the same fields as the daemon's.

files.note: Adds headOf, suiteOf, and cancelledOf, and rewrites checksOf to count every time.

checks.text: Open review finding: only the failed check runs of a cancelled run move to cancelled. A job that passed before the cancel still counts as passing, so a head whose only run had a passed job reads checks passing, not the checks cancelled that docs/plugins.md describes. The same line applies the rule the daemon's finding describes, so a failure before the cancel is hidden here too.

files.note: A table of rollups: a newer run that passed, one still running, nothing run since, and a cancelled run beside a real failure in another workflow.

groups.title: The panel draws the cancelled and draft notes
groups.kicker: What a row and its drawer show
intro: A row's notes, the words after its title, now end with cancelled, muted, while isCancelled holds. A draft whose word another status takes, such as conflict, also gets an italic draft note, because its italic number alone is easy to miss. The drawer's checks read checks cancelled in the muted color.

files.note: Adds the cancelled color, the optional note color and italic, and the two new notes.

Adds a pull request whose only run a label cancelled, and checks the row reads ready with a muted cancelled note and checks cancelled in the drawer, and that a conflicting draft notes draft in italic.

groups.title: Documentation
groups.kicker: The CLI guide and the panel's reference
intro: docs/cli.md gains "Keep review labels from cancelling CI runs", which advises leaving labeled out of the checks' workflow and shows a separate workflow for a label that should start a fuller run. The CHECKS row of the events table and the panel's states, notes, and drawer checks in docs/plugins.md describe the new behavior.
